issues.text: The specification for the header (RFC 9111) defines max-age twice: s5.2.1.1 as a request directive and s5.2.2.1 as a response directive. Searching the page for max-age lands first on the request directive (TOC L99, body L1116, before L1208), so "the paragraph that defines it" is ambiguous; the line copied from the script is a response header.
issues.quote: search the page for `max-age`, the word before the `=` in the line you copied, and read only the paragraph that defines it
issues.fix: Change to: "search the page for `max-age`, the word before the `=` in the line you copied, and read only the paragraph that defines it for a response, since the line you copied came from a response." Update the VI text the same way. No claim change needed.

issues.text: This paragraph packs four steps (search the site; for a header search the spec; note its number and check for a newer one; how the RFC page shows that) into one block. I read it twice to separate 'what to search' from 'how to check the number'.
issues.quote: Its version is its number: note it and check that no newer number obsoletes or updates it; if one does, open the newer number and read that instead.
issues.fix: Split the paragraph after 'search for its specification by name.' so the number check and the 'This RFC is now obsolete' / 'Updated by' lines form their own short paragraph.

issues.text: Step 2 says to open the official page for the header's specification, and section 4 says 'search for its specification by name', but I do not know which name to type (the header's? 'Cache-Control RFC'?) nor how to tell the official RFC page from other sites that copy or describe it.
issues.quote: Then open the official reference page for that header — for a standard header, that page is its specification
issues.fix: Add one clause to step 2: search the header name together with 'RFC', and pick the page that shows an RFC number and the 'obsolete' / 'Updated by' lines at its top, as section 4 describes.
